sentences.text: The genus name Daanosaurus translates to "Da'an lizard," referencing the Da'an district in Sichuan, China.
The only known specimen, the holotype — the specific fossil used to define the species — is a partial skeleton belonging to a juvenile individual.
Based on this young skeleton, scientists estimate that adults reached 18 meters in length, stood 9 meters high, and weighed 30 tonnes.
The type species Daanosaurus zhangi was formally described in 2005 from fossils recovered in the Upper Shaximiao Formation.
The species name zhangi honors Zhang Aiping, the former Minister of National Defense, while the genus name refers to the Da'an district where the fossils were found.
Daanosaurus was originally classified in the subfamily Bellusaurinae, which is part of the family Brachiosauridae.
Recent studies have placed Daanosaurus in the clade Macronaria based on opisthocoelous posterior dorsal vertebrae, a trait also found in mamenchisaurids.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Daanosaurus as Mamenchisauridae.
Daanosaurus is considered by many to be a eusauropod due to its similarity to Bellusaurus.
Daanosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Jurassic, approximately 156 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
The estimated time range for this animal spans from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Daanosaurus may be a mamenchisaurid, though this classification remains debated due to the juvenile nature of the fossil.
